text:
ajay: Quick handover — INC-4723 (inference host instability) is still active, paging started ~22:10 UTC. Root cause unknown; symptoms: intermittent OOMs on model-worker-3, elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate, tail latency spikes. I've been driving for the last 45m. Current state: we've paused background batch jobs, rolled back a recent config bump to 256 tokens, and added a temporary 1GB swap on the node which dropped immediate OOMs but errors persist. Primary metrics dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/inc/4723 (read-only).

ajay: Ownership I'd like to transfer: driver -> maria, comms -> kevin. Secondary/backup -> sophia. Reason: I'm hitting my limit for the night and have a call in 10m. If anyone objects speak now.

incident-bot: [auto] Pager triggered for INC-4723 at 2026-03-14T22:09:52Z. Current on-call: ajay. Escalation policy: eng-sre -> eng-runtime.

maria: I can take driver. Thanks for the notes. Quick clarifying Qs: did rollback revert the kernel hint patch or only the runtime token cap? Also which cluster node IDs are still showing OOMs? I saw worker-3 and worker-7 in the alert but your note only mentions worker-3.

ajay: rollback only reverted the token cap change (runtime config). Kernel hint patch is not deployed to prod. Alerts tied to worker-3 and worker-7; worker-7 had a transient CPU cap event but hasn't OOM'd since we throttled batches. worker-3 still shows OOM traces in dmesg.

maria: ok. Plan I'm taking: 1) assume driver; 2) confirm if we need to cordon worker-3 and failover; 3) if failover doesn't recover within 10m, spin up replacement node from dedicated pool and route traffic. Kevin, if you can own comms please draft a short status update for the customer-facing channel and the status page. Use the templated outage note in the runbook.

kevin: on comms. I'll publish a short "degraded performance on inference" note and link our incident postmortem doc. I'll set cadence updates every 15m until resolved. Drafting now: "We're investigating elevated errors and latency for inference endpoints. No data leak detected. Next update in 15m." Want me to post to status.redwood? (yes/no)

sophia: I'm on standby for secondary. If maria wants me to take live metrics or rotate canary traffic, say the word. Also note: APAC coverage gap at 03:00 UTC — if this runs past that we need to trigger the handover protocol in the oncall rota.

maria: please take metrics, sophia. Kevin: post to status.redwood and slack #customers:status. Use the runbook template header: "Short summary, user impact, mitigation steps taken, next steps, ETA". I'll attach logs later.

maria: immediate actions I'm running now:

```
# check OOMs on worker-3
ssh admin@worker-3 "sudo journalctl -u model-worker -n 200 | rg OOM"
# verify KV cache sizes
curl -s "https://internal.api/metrics?node=worker-3" | jq '.kv_cache'
# cordon node (if needed)
kubectl cordon node/worker-3 && kubectl drain node/worker-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

ajay: FYI I already pulled the sakura snapshot and uploaded it to /incidents/4723/snapshots. If you need it for analysis it's there. Also note we have a temporary quota increase with cloud team if we need to spin up replacements quickly.

incident-bot: [auto] Incident INC-4723 updated: driver=maria, comms=kevin, secondary=sophia.

kevin: status posted to status.redwood and #customers:status. Link: https://status.redwood/incident/4723. Message: "Investigating elevated errors and latency for inference endpoints. We're routing around affected nodes; updates every 15m." Added :loudspeaker: and pinged affected customers list.

maria: after cordon I'm seeing steady reduction in 5xx on the main route but tail latency still elevated by ~120ms. Next step: if latency doesn't drop under 50ms within 10m, we will start replacing worker-3 from the dedicated pool and scale the canary group down/up to rebalance connections.

sophia: noted. I'll prepare the canary scale command and be ready to execute: `./deploy/bin/scale_canary --group inference-canary -n 3` and monitor connection metrics.

maria: also flagging possible customer impact: batch jobs for partner X might see failed requests; CS + support already notified via DM. No evidence of data exfil yet. Keep confidentiality on logs — scrub PII before attaching publicly.

ajay: thanks team — leaving the bridge now. Maria, Kevin, Sophia you have control. I will be reachable by DM in case of quick clarifications.

maria: taking driver. I'll update the incident doc with timeline and assign follow-ups. If anyone sees a regression after node replacement, escalate to eng-runtime oncall and open a follow-up ticket.

kevin: will continue cadence updates. tagging ops-sre for visibility. :thumbsup:

sophia: standby for canary ops. Good handoff. :white_check_mark:
